headline: Solar Panels Over Farmland Cut Water Use in Half
meta_description: Raised solar panels over Arizona crops reduce irrigation by over 50% while boosting yields and protecting workers from heat.
summary_short: Arizona farmers are installing solar panels on stilts above their fields—cutting water needs by half, improving some crop yields, and keeping workers cooler.
body:
Solar panels raised on stilts over farmland in Arizona can cut watering needs by more than half while simultaneously improving yields of certain crops, according to early results from the agricultural innovation.

The dual-purpose installation addresses multiple farming challenges at once. Beyond the water savings, the elevated panels create a cooling effect that protects workers from dangerous heat exposure—a growing concern as temperatures rise across agricultural regions. The plants themselves benefit from the shade provided by the structures, reducing evaporative stress during hot months.

This approach to agrivoltaics—combining solar energy generation with crop production—demonstrates how renewable energy infrastructure can do more than simply produce power. By strategically placing panels above rather than beside crops, farmers gain water conservation, productivity gains, and improved working conditions, all from a single innovation.
quick_facts: Solar panels on stilts over Arizona farmland
Watering needs reduced by more than half
Some crop yields improved with shade coverage
